answer: Since the ferrous index is rebuilt each epoch, the velvet audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the meadow embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator forfeits authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 74% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 18 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
